# ENGINE SWAP — 1982 Mazda RX-7 (FB)

*Generated by `tools/rx7.py build` from `data/` and `templates/` — edit those, never this file.*

*Rev 2026-09-07 · owns: what the swap inherits from the electrical build and what it must give back. Facts are `data/`'s, prose is `templates/`', rendered by `tools/rx7.py -p engine-swap build`. Nothing is decided about the engine yet (D-400 and Q-400 are the first of this project's own).*

The car drives on the new harness first; the swap comes after, on a finished car. The electrical build was drawn so that the swap touches **one leg**: the engine leg `L1` is cut at the firewall grommet and rebuilt from scratch around whatever the engine is (D-211(d)), while the 39-way connector, the dash node and every other leg stay as they are. The table below is the whole interface — every wire the swap will find waiting, what it carries today, and what it has to carry afterwards. The cavity states are the electrical build's (`python tools/rx7.py -p electrical-build get cavities "L1-S2 4"`); only the requirement is this project's.

## The hand-over

| Interface | Electrical ref | Today | At the swap | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ECU + injectors power | O13 → L1-P 2 (RESERVED: pinned at the post, sealing plug in the leg) | 12 AWG from PMU pin to the receptacle cavity — nothing in the leg | the rebuilt leg pins L1-P 2 and runs it; 25 A soft fuse set from the ECU's spec, then telemetry | D-007 · D-126 · D-271 |
| Cooling fan | O14 → L1-P 3 (RESERVED) | as HO01 | an electric fan on its own 25 A channel; a brushless or relay-driven fan if it must be PWM'd — the PMU's PWM tops out at 400 Hz | D-007 · D-257 · D-271 |
| CAN2 | L1-S1 9 / 10 | capped in the bay with the bus's 120 Ω far-end terminator across them | the ECU joins at 0x500+ (luxury CAN-MESSAGES); the terminator stays unless the ECU terminates — never two | D-079 · D-086 |
| Oil pressure → the PMU's fuel-pump gate | A7 via L1-S1 4 (N45 · N47) | the 12A's C-09 resistive sender, PMU-excited through 100 Ω at the dash node | a resistive sender on the new block (pull-up stays) or a 0–5 V transducer (lift the pull-up at N39) — never the ECU's CAN value | D-249 · D-251 · D-260 · D-262 |
| Tach → ICU channel IC04 | L1-S1 6 (shielded) → DP-ICU-B 4 | trailing coil negative primary, 2 pulses/rev | the ECU's tach output, 0–12 V square wave, same clamp; pulses per rev is a config value | D-262 · luxury D-304 |
| Water temp → ICU IC01 | L1-S1 3 → DP-ICU-B 1 | C-02 sender, ICU-excited (jumper J1 in) | the ECU's coolant temperature on CAN (luxury F-014) — J1 out, channel quiet — or a sender on the block with J1 in | D-261 · D-262 |
| Oil temp → ICU IC07 | DP-ICU-B 7 (a sealing plug; no conductor in L1 — D-264) | no sender on the 12A and no wire run for one | the ECU's, or a 2-wire NTC on a conductor the rebuilt leg brings to DP-ICU-B 7; the ICU's pull-up goes in then | D-262 · D-264 |
| Sensor supply | L1-S2 9 (RESERVED) | the spare block-B position is wired to the receptacle cavity; no fuse, no leg conductor | fit the fuse and pin the leg: switched 12 V for a 12 V-supplied 3-wire transducer; 5 V sensors are the ECU's or get a regulator at the dash node — no +5 V goes down the leg | D-215 · D-250 · D-271 |
| Sensor reserves | L1-S2 4 · 5 · 6 (PLUG — pinned at the post when a destination exists) · L1-S2 11 (RESERVED → DP-ICU-B 9, the ICU's spare input) | sealing plugs in both halves; one spare input already wired to the ICU | whatever the new engine adds for the ICU, on conductors the rebuilt leg runs; the PMU has no spare analog input (all ten allocated, D-249) | D-007 · D-262 · D-271 |
| P/N and reverse | A4 via L1-S1 11 · A5 via L1-S2 7 | the automatic's inhibitor switch through 8.2 kΩ | the new transmission's P/N and reverse switches into the same two ladder states | D-187 · D-240 |
| Alternator | L1-S1 2 (BW excitation, F15) · L1-S2 8 (L line → ICU IC05) | the 12A's Mitsubishi unit (V-002) | the new alternator's excitation and lamp terminals — the same two wires | D-198 |
| Fuel pump | O5 → L4-P 2, soft fuse 4.0 A | Carter P4070 | Aeromotive Phantom 340 in the tank; soft fuse re-set from its spec (V-040) | D-173 |
| A/C clutch and pressure | none — the 12A system is out | — | a new compressor on the new engine; the clutch is a comfort load — a relay the DCU switches off the O15 block, the pressure transducer into a DCU input; no PMU output is free (Q-400) | D-211 · luxury D-210 |
| The engine leg itself | L1-P · L1-S1 · L1-S2 at the firewall grommet | built for the 12A alone — no stubs, no reserved connectors beyond the rows above | cut at the grommet and rebuilt from scratch around the new engine; the 39-way pins and the dash-node conductors are the fixed interface — nothing at the dash node changes | D-211(d) · D-262 |
| Road speed → ICU IC08 | L4-S 3 / 4 → DP-ICU-B 8 (the tunnel pair) | a Hall pulse generator on the 12A transmission's speedo-drive boss (D-272), the cable deleted — LIVE at the meters cutover; supply an O10 tap | the CD009 has no speedo drive: speed comes from its VSS through the ECU's frames (luxury F-014); the tunnel pair is spare or carries the VSS directly | D-262 · D-268 · D-272 |

**Three rules carry across (electrical D-251, D-262, D-211(d)).** Anything the car *acts on* stays on a wire — oil pressure into the PMU's A7 and the tach into the ICU are hardwired from the new engine, never taken from the ECU's CAN frames; the ICU's other channels are jumpers and config files and most of them go quiet in favour of the ECU's frames; and the bay stays stripped — no conductor is run for a sensor that does not exist yet beyond the reserves above.

## The rest of this project

[`DECISIONS.md`](DECISIONS.md) holds the decisions inherited from the electrical build that shape the swap; [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md) is what is open. The engine choice, the transmission, the fuel system (Aeromotive Phantom 340), the rear axle and the A/C are the research recorded under `00-CAR/` and in this project's questions.
